action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. The next few days call for care in applying it: price is about 6% under its 50-day average and has been for 14 days, it is down about 5% over the week, the mood is still fearful at 34 out of 100, and exchange safety is still in the news after the Binance and Mercado Bitcoin thefts. So add spend only in small steps, lead with safety and trust rather than hard offers, keep part of the increase ready to pause, and speed up only once price wins back about $81,951. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($76,988) is about 5% above its 200-day average ($73,171), which is still rising.

watch: The long-run trend still points up, but price has spent two weeks under its 50-day average while many people keep betting on a rise with borrowed money. A close above $78,250 would steady things, while a close below $75,750 puts the $73,171 average in focus.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the last few weeks have been weak and the short term is soft to neutral. Bitcoin has now closed under its 50-day average for 14 days, sits about 6% below it and about 10% under its 30-day high, though the mood recovered a little, with Fear & Greed at 34 after 26 a day earlier. A normal week swings about $2,630, so a close above $78,250 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $75,750 (bottom of that swing) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; for the bigger picture, $73,171 (the 200-day average) is the floor. Binance reopening withdrawals for more coins is offset by Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin still being closed after its theft, so keep leading with trust rather than offers until price steadies.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 20% higher and about 87% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 10%. Price must win back $81,951 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. News adds a little here, with South Korea planning to make exchanges keep 99% of customer coins offline and the US futures regulator allowing a crypto-style contract on regulated exchanges; the US jobs report is due on 6 November and the next Fed meeting is 8 December, so save bigger campaign pushes for that reclaim.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 5% above its 200-day average and that average is still rising, about 4% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 38% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,171 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,533 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. News is nudging this up a little, led by Shopify and Coinbase building digital-dollar payments for online shops, and a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
